Predicting from a network regression, and its terms

Source: R/interpret_predict.R
predict_mrqap.Rd

predict() gives the predicted value of the outcome for each dyad.

  • For an infernetMrqapFit, from estimate_mrqap(), it predicts either the dyads that the model was fitted on, or the dyads of newdata.

  • For a netlm or netlogit, from net_regression() in {migraph} before 2.0.0, it predicts the rows of a design matrix.

formula() and terms() of an infernetMrqapFit give the formula that was fitted and the columns of its coefficients.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'infernetMrqapFit'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, type = c("link", "response"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlm'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlogit'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, type = c("link", "response"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'infernetMrqapFit'
formula(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'infernetMrqapFit'
terms(x, ...)

Arguments

object

An infernetMrqapFit object, as returned by estimate_mrqap(), or a netlm or netlogit object.

newdata

The dyads to predict. For an infernetMrqapFit, NULL (the default) predicts the dyads that the model was fitted on. Otherwise, a data frame or a matrix with a column for each predictor, named as the coefficients are, e.g. ego_Citations. A column for an interaction, e.g. ego_Age:same_Grp, is computed from its parts where it is absent. The model's own dyad-level data, object$pred, has these columns. A matrix without column names needs a column for each coefficient, in their order, with the intercept first. For a netlm or netlogit, a design matrix with the same columns as the fitted model.

type

The scale of the predictions: "link" (the default), the scale of the linear predictor, or "response", the scale of the outcome, e.g. probabilities for a binomial model and expected counts for a count model. For a gaussian model the two are the same.

...

Not used.

x

For formula() and terms(), an infernetMrqapFit, from estimate_mrqap().

Value

A numeric vector of predicted values, one for each dyad or row.

formula() of a fit gives a formula, and terms() a terms object.

Details

Without newdata, the prediction for an infernetMrqapFit is the fitted value of each dyad of the model, with any random intercepts and absorbed fixed effects.

With newdata, the prediction comes from the coefficients only. A random intercept is then zero, as for a dyad of a node the model has not seen. A fixed effect is absorbed, so it has no coefficient, and a model with fixed effects predicts only the dyads it was fitted on. For a zero-inflated Poisson model, the zero-inflation part reads the same columns as the count part.

The formula and the terms of a fit

formula() of a fit from estimate_mrqap() gives the formula that was fitted, after specify_mrqap() read it, and terms() gives the terms of the columns that were fitted, as the coefficients name them. These are the columns that newdata needs, and that each coefficient is the effect of. For the formula of chosen rows of a table of terms, see specify_terms.

See also

Other interpreting functions: play_diffusions(), simulate_mrqap, sweep

Examples

networkers <- manynet::ison_networkers |>
  manynet::to_subgraph(Discipline == "Sociology")
model1 <- estimate_mrqap(weight ~ ego(Citations) + alter(Citations),
                         networkers, times = 5)
# The fitted value of each dyad
head(predict(model1))
#> [1] 2.870599 2.404405 3.089984 2.020481 2.239866 3.035138
# A sender with 10 citations, to a receiver with 50
predict(model1, data.frame(ego_Citations = 10, alter_Citations = 50))
#> [1] 2.650721
fit <- estimate_mrqap(advice ~ same(dept) + reports,
                      manynet::ison_hightech, times = 5)
formula(fit)
#> advice ~ same(dept) + reports
#> <environment: 0x87d43dc78>
terms(fit)
#> advice ~ same_dept + reports
#> attr(,"variables")
#> list(advice, same_dept, reports)
#> attr(,"factors")
#>           same_dept reports
#> advice            0       0
#> same_dept         1       0
#> reports           0       1
#> attr(,"term.labels")
#> [1] "same_dept" "reports"  
#> attr(,"order")
#> [1] 1 1
#> attr(,"intercept")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,"response")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,".Environment")
#> <environment: 0x8875d1188>
